properties.description: Built by the Weeden brothers, this was the home of the nomadic Menlo French Laundry. The laundry, established in 1893 by the Larrecou family had a special relationship with Jane Stanford. Feldman Books was located in this building until 2018.
Built by the Weeden brothers, this building was occupied for many years by Menlo Meat Market (Harry and Margaret Doughty) and later by Gentry Magazine.

properties.name: Trinity Chapel
properties.description: The redwood chapel, formerly located on Encinal Ave was moved to this, Pine St location in 1897. Then the chapel was moved to 1220 Crane St in 1957.

properties.sources: Goldston, Linda, “San Jose will lose another cannery — and 205 jobs”, San Jose Mercury News, 18 December 1982, p. 8B

properties.name: John T Doyle Home
properties.description: John T Doyle, the son of Irish immigrants, built a two story home in 1868. He became an attorney in San Francisco. He and his wife, Antonia, raised 5 children here.

properties.name: Linden Towers, Flood Mansion
properties.description: James C Flood's mansion was completed in 1878 after 3 years of construction. James lived there until his death in 1889, when it was inherited by his daughter, Jennie, who donated it to the Univ of California. Home's contents were sold at auction in 1934.
properties.sources: Flood Property Atherton By: James & Waters - Rumsey Map Collection

properties.name: Oak Grove Villa Hotel
properties.description: 2nd hotel in MP. It became the first building in Menlo Park to be lit by gas lamps when the SF Gas and Electric Co. extended pipelines down the peninsula alongside the RR tracks from South San Francisco in 1907.

properties.name: Faxon Dean Atherton Residence
properties.description: Faxon Dean Atherton, a successful "merchant prince" in Valparaiso, Chile, moved his family to SF in 1860. By 1861 he completed this estate, called "Valparaiso Park."  The house was used as a school for a year before it burned down in 1902.

properties.name: Fire House
properties.description: The original small wooden building was stored in the MP Fire Dept on Middlefield Rd.

properties.name: Golder's Menlo Park House
properties.description: First business established in Menlo Park featured a saloon. On the same site as the first fire station and later Dieter's Auto Repair. Building was split and one part moved to 1340 El Camino Real, other part lost to fire.

properties.name: Fremont School
properties.description: Closed in 1971, demolished in 2000

properties.name: St. Bridgit's School
properties.description: The first school in Menlo Park (1872) was in St. Bridgit’s Catholic Church (now Nativity), then located on Middlefield Road opposite Ravenswood Ave., thus in today’s Atherton.

properties.name: Ravenswood
properties.description: Ravenswood is named after Isaiah Churchill Woods, a wealthy SF businessman who in 1852 acquired about 2000 acres in MP. He erected a pre-fab home, named  it "Woodside Dairy."(it was shipped around the horn) in the area of today's Menlo Oaks neighborhood.

properties.name: St Bridget's Chapel
properties.description: The chapel was transported on log rollers from Ringwood Avenue to Santa Cruz Ave. A year later, in 1878, it was moved again to its present location on Oak Grove Ave. These three moves prompted a local wit to call Nativity "the roamin' Catholic Church”.

properties.name: St. Dennis Church
properties.description: St. Dennis Church, San Mateo County’s first church, built in 1853 by Dennis Martin

properties.description: The brick Duff & Doyle building was repaired after the 1906 earthquake and operated until 1922 when the business was liquidated. Menlo Grocery used the building in the 1920 and 30s.

properties.name: YWCA Hostess House
properties.description: This building was a Hostess House built by the Y.W.C.A. for troops at Camp Fremont in Menlo Park during World War I. It was moved to this location, used as a community center and then renovated as a restaurant in 1981.

properties.name: Veterans Administrationm
properties.description: This building was a Hostess House built by the Y.W.C.A. for troops at Camp Fremont in Menlo Park during World War I. It was moved to this location, used as a community center and then renovated as a restaurant in 1981.

properties.name: Guardhouse
properties.description: An a crossing guard in the guardhouse would lower a wooden arm to block pedestrian and carriage traffic from crossing the tracks when the train was approaching the station.  The guardhouse was located on hotel property.

properties.name: Thurlow Lodge / Sherwood Hall
properties.description: US Senator, Milton Latham bought the Barron estate and mansion in 1871. The mansion accidentally burned down during renovation. Latham built a new and larger 3 story mansion with 98 ft tower, calling it Thurlow Lodge.
properties.sources: Menlo Parh Histrorical Assn | 1907-1917 Stanford Park Real Estate Map

properties.name: Barron Mansion
properties.description: William E Barron built a 40 room, 2 story mansion with a 3 story tower in 1864. Barron also installed an artificial trout pond, a large grapery, an enclosed deer park, and an ornamental fountain in front of his newly built mansion.

properties.name: Holm Grove
properties.description: Prominent banker, Joseph A Donahoe built Holm Grove in 1868 on Middlefield and Ringwood Road. In 1949, the Donahoe sold the property to the City of Menlo Park for the construction of Menlo Atherton High School.

properties.name: Main Building
properties.description: Construction begins June 1 1897. School opens on Aug 1 1898. Main Building is damaged in 1906 earthquake. Building is remodeled and expanded to 3 stories and re-opened in 1915.

properties.name: Rosso Residence
properties.description: Rosso family home, built in 1924 for John (Giovanni) Rosso and wife Annunziata nee Ardizzoia. In 1930 they lived here with 3 daughters.

properties.name: Blanchard Residence
properties.description: Addie (nee Francis Scarpa) and Bertrand Blanchard moved to Menlo Park in 1880. He opened one of the town's first butcher shops. They had 7 kids by 1900. She died here at age 84 in June 1936. The house had 5 different occupants over the next 10 years.
Bldg appears on aerial photo from about 1947-1950.

properties.name: Guild Theater
properties.description: Originally built as a burlesque house and converted to exhibit movies in the 1940’s. It was renamed Guild Theatre on March 30, 1948. It was operated by Landmark Theaters until 2018.

properties.name: Menlo Theater
properties.description: Originally built as a burlesque house and converted to exhibit movies in the 1940’s. It was renamed Guild Theatre on March 30, 1948. The theater lost 30 feet of its entrance lobby during the expansion of El Camino Real in the 1930s.

properties.name: Sharon Heights Mansion
properties.description: The Sharon Estate came from the notorious Gilded Age mining tycoon and Nevada Representative, William Sharon. The building was razed for the development of Sharon Heights.
